messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can we simply sample from the joint gaussian distribution using NUTS in Stan?
parts:
Yes, but ti's a bad idea. Just draw independent samples
from the multi-normal if that's all you're trying to do.

The Stan program to draw from a multivariate normal using
NUTS is trivial:

data {
int N;
vector[N] mu;
cov_matrix[N] Sigma;
}
parameters {
vector[N] y;
}
model {
y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

But it's far far better to do this:

generated quantities {
vector[N] y = multi_normal_rng(mu, Sigma);
}

to draw independent samples.

- Bob

> On Mar 16, 2017, at 6:30 PM, Hamed Nikbakht <hamednik...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I have a conceptual problem about the Stan and i couldn't find my answer through the Stan's manual or other related documents.
>
> Can we simply sample from the joint gaussian distribution using NUTS in Stan? I'm asking it because we can do it simply through other MCMC techniques like Gibbs sampling and metropolis-hasting algorithms.
> I was more into frequentist approach but it looks everything in Stan is based on Bayesian approach.
>
> I'm studying like about 2 weeks on and off about the Stan but still some parts of it is unclear to me conceptually.
>
> My big concern in my research is having efficient sampling while simultaneously keeping the samples independent effectively. and i found through the paper of Hoffman& Gelman that NUTS is doing that using the Hamiltonian MC algorithm.
> and it can be more efficient computationally than metropolis MCMC and Gibbs and everything in NUTS will be automated in terms of step size and other parameters using dual averaging technique.
>
> I'm trying to understand what Stan is exactly doing. I would appreciate it if you could write this toy example here which help me a lot for understanding better.
>
> Thank you very much in advance for your help.
>
> Regards,
> Hamed

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can we simply sample from the joint gaussian distribution using NUTS in Stan?
parts:
It won't work. HMC visits tail regions proportional to
their probability mass (assuming the tails aren't too fat).
It just does it more slowly than independent samplers.

- Bob

>
> I think directly sampling from the multi-normal distribution quite often visiting the typical set space, which computationally it might not be reasonable.
>

but it doesn't give me any sample just showing an empty set after less than one sec.

Am i doing something wrong?

My Stan code:

data {
  int N;
  vector[N] mu;
  cov_matrix[N] Sigma;
}
parameters {
  vector[N] y;
}
model {
  y ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

n=1000; % Dimension of the problem
mu = zeros(1,n);
Sigma = eye(n);
MCMC_dat = struct('N',n,'mu',mu,'Sigma',Sigma);
fit = stan('file','MN2.stan','data',MCMC_dat,'chains',1,'iter',100,'algorithm','NUTS');

I attach the screenshot of the results after run as well.

Thank you

Hamed

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can we simply sample from the joint gaussian distribution using NUTS in Stan?
parts:
No. Because there won't be any draws in the tail
regions!

And as to the other question, you have to wait for Stan to
compile the model. But it's *not* going to do what you want!

- Bob

> On Mar 18, 2017, at 7:42 PM, Hamed Nikbakht <hamednik...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Can we mixed up the importance sampling technique with Stan to give more mass to the tail regions? (To have less coefficient of variation (C.O.V) comparing with the pure MC simulation)
>
> (I tried the Metropolis-Hasting MCMC using different threshold levels to reach the tail regions and it works pretty well comparing with the pure MC simulation).
>
> The whole question is not related to Stan but some part of it is associated with the Stan application.
>
> Thank you very much.
>
> - Hamed
